content: Word Error Rate (WER) is a common metric to evaluate ASR performance. It is measured as the sum of errors (insertions, deletions and substitutions) divided by the total number of words in the reference transcription. As we are investigating the impact on performance of speaker's gender and role, we computed the WER for each speaker at the episode (show occurrence) level. Analyzing at such granularity allows us to avoid large WER variation that could be observed at utterance level (especially for short speech turns) but also makes possible to get several WER values for a given speaker, one for each occurrence of a show in which he/she appears on. Speaker's gender was provided by the meta-data and role was obtained using the criteria from Section SECREF6 computed for each show. This enables us to analyze our results across gender and role categories which was done using Wilcoxon rank sum tests also called Mann-Whitney U test (with $\alpha $= 0.001) BIBREF30. The choice of a Wilcoxon rank sum test and not the commonly used t-test is motivated by the non-normality of our data.
